newsitem.title: CANADA: Repap says has liquidity through to Q3.
newsitem.headline: Repap says has liquidity through to Q3.

text.p: Stephen Larson, president and chief operating officer of Repap Enterprises Inc said on Monday that the company's liquidity situation has been resolved through to "well into" its third quarter.
In an interview, Larson told Reuters that the company has enough financial liquidity to maintain operations and meet bond and interest payments through to the third quarter.

"The liquidity situation is resolved for the interim period," Larson told Reuters in an interview. "Of course, it depends on the continuation of the improvement that we are seeing in the coated paper markets."
"The rumors of some type of corporate filing are not true. We will not be making any such filing," he said.

Earlier on Monday, Repap said that while its board of directors would prefer to sell all of the company's shares, it is prepared to consider bids of each and any combination of the company's operations. Larson said that since Repap began looking for the buyers for the entire company last summer, several potential bidders indicated a preference to make offers only on specific assets.
"I think it is quite probable that at least one will be sold and that probably will be Manitoba," he said.

Larson said the Manitoba operations, which consist of a 170,000-ton kraft paper mill and sawmill, have been "consistently profitable," but are not considered part of the company's coated paper core business.
But Larson said he would not rule out selling all of Repap.
"Going forward, the sale process of the entire company still could very well be a possibility," he said.
Larson said he is confident that Repap will be able to meet its objectives in selling all or parts of the company.
"I am quite confident that we can meet these objectives. The assets are quite well known, they are operating well and the (paper) market is quite strong," Larson said.
Larson said Repap's operating units in Manitoba and Wisconsin have enough financial liquidity to maintain operations.
A C$20 million increase in the bank credit line provided by Toronto-Dominion Bank for Repap's operating unit in New Brunswick will be sufficient to meet its liquidity needs, Larson said.

Larson said Repap does not envisage filing for bankruptcy protection through to the third quarter, by which time it hopes to have completed the process of selling all or parts of the company's operations.
